video.title: Minnesota Timberwolves 2026/27 Season Preview: Going For It With LaMelo Ball

summary: Josh Lloyd and Ben Beacon (Locked On Wolves) preview the 2026/27 Minnesota Timberwolves after the trade that brought in LaMelo Ball and sent out Julius Randle and Naz Reid. Ben expects Anthony Edwards to move off the ball more, which should mean more catch-and-shoot threes, while LaMelo runs the offense. The fifth starter is still open. Ben guesses Josh Green over Ayo Dosunmu, with Trey Lyles and later rookie Joan Beringer as power forward options. Donte DiVincenzo is out until about March. Ben says LaMelo's health decides the team's ceiling, and he predicts 53 wins. Josh warns that Minnesota has a two-game week in the middle of every possible fantasy playoff window, so Edwards and Ball should drop slightly in close draft decisions.

rules.text: Check fantasy playoff schedules. If a team has a two-game week during the fantasy playoffs, move its players down a little when choosing between them and similar players.
rules.quote: if there's tiebre decisions between Anthony Edwards and someone else, Lamelo Ball and someone else, drop them down a little bit

rules.text: Minnesota has a two-game week in the middle of the fantasy playoffs no matter which weeks a head-to-head league uses, so it is hard to avoid.
rules.quote: No matter what sort of week you're choosing to have your playoffs, there's a twoame week for them.

rules.text: League quality is up and tanking incentives are down. That could mean fewer easy wins late in the season and lower win totals for good teams.
rules.quote: The tanking incentives are down and what that does to team win totals

player_notes.text: Traded to Minnesota. He is expected to run the offense and handle the ball much more than Edwards.

team_notes.text: Traded Julius Randle and Naz Reid for LaMelo Ball and moved to a smaller, guard-heavy lineup. Kyle Anderson, Mike Conley, Joe Ingles and Julian Phillips are gone.

team_notes.text: Four starters are set: Ball, Edwards, McDaniels and Gobert. The fifth spot is open and could depend on matchups, though Finch rarely changes starters unless someone is hurt.
team_notes.quote: The Wolves typically don't switch up their starting lineup unless there's an injury.

team_notes.text: Bench depth is thin and there is little scoring punch off the bench. The team is short on size and defensive rebounding.
team_notes.quote: they're just not going to have enough defensive rebounding if they don't play a little bit bigger

team_notes.text: Ben expects a top 10 defense and, if LaMelo stays healthy, a top 10 offense. He predicts 53 wins.
team_notes.quote: So, I I'm going to go 53 wins, I think. And they won 49 each the last two years.
